assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Supernova
items.clue: The explosion of a massive star.

items.label: Nebula
items.clue: A cloud of dust and gas in space.

items.label: Planet
items.clue: A large body in orbit around the Sun.

items.label: Red giant
items.clue: The stage a star about the size of the Sun swells into when it leaves the main sequence.

questions.stem: Which list correctly describes what our solar system contains?

options.text: One star, the eight planets, the dwarf planets and the planets' moons
One star and the eight planets that orbit around it, nothing else
One star, nine planets including Pluto, and the moons of those
Eight planets and their moons, with the Sun counted as a planet

questions.explanation: This is exactly the membership the specification gives: one star, the Sun, the eight planets, the dwarf planets, and the natural satellites that orbit planets.

questions.stem: What is meant by a natural satellite?

options.text: A small rocky body that orbits the Sun directly, between the planets
A dwarf planet, which orbits the Sun beyond the eight planets
A moon: a body that orbits a planet rather than orbiting the Sun
A man-made craft kept in orbit by its engines, not gravity

questions.explanation: The specification defines natural satellites as the moons that orbit planets, and states that they are part of the solar system.

questions.stem: Which statement describes how our solar system relates to the Milky Way?

options.text: The Milky Way is just another name for our own solar system
Our solar system is a small part of the Milky Way galaxy
The Milky Way galaxy holds everything in the universe
Our solar system lies at the exact centre of the Milky Way

questions.explanation: The specification states directly that our solar system is a small part of the Milky Way galaxy.

options.text: From a cloud of dust and gas squeezed together by magnetism
From a huge ball of chemical fuel that was set alight in space
From a cloud of dust and gas in which fusion started at once
From a cloud of dust and gas pulled together by gravity

questions.explanation: The specification states that the Sun was formed from a cloud of dust and gas (nebula) pulled together by gravitational attraction.

questions.stem: At the start of a star's life cycle, why do fusion reactions begin?

options.text: Gravity draws the dust and gas together, heating it until nuclei fuse
The dust and gas catch fire and burn chemically, giving out the energy
Fusion starts as soon as gravity begins to draw the cloud inwards
Magnetic forces squeeze the cloud until its particles join together

questions.explanation: Gravitational attraction pulls the material of the nebula together; the compression raises the temperature and density until fusion reactions start.

questions.stem: Which two effects are in equilibrium in a stable star?

options.text: No effects at all, because equilibrium means no forces act on it
The inward pull of gravity and the outward push of gravity itself
The weight of the star and the upthrust of the gas around it
The gravitational collapse inwards and the expansion due to fusion energy

questions.explanation: The specification states that fusion reactions lead to an equilibrium between the gravitational collapse of a star and its expansion due to fusion energy.

questions.stem: A main sequence star stays the same size for billions of years. Why?

options.text: No forces act inside a star once it reaches the main sequence
Its inward collapse and its outward expansion stay balanced
Gravity pushes the star outwards as hard as it pulls it inwards
The upthrust of the gas around it supports the star's weight

questions.explanation: While fusion continues at a steady rate, the expansion due to fusion energy exactly balances the gravitational collapse, so the star's size does not change.

questions.stem: A straight copper rod lies horizontally between the poles of a strong magnet. Which action induces a potential difference across the ends of the rod?

options.text: Moving the rod steadily downwards through the magnetic field
Holding the rod still between the poles of a strong magnet
Joining the ends of the rod with a length of copper wire
Warming the rod so that its resistance rises a little

questions.explanation: The conductor moves relative to the magnetic field, so a potential difference is induced across the ends of the rod.

questions.stem: An alternator and a dynamo are both turned steadily by the same motor. How do their outputs differ?

options.text: The dynamo generates ac and the alternator generates dc
Both generate ac, though the dynamo's output is larger
The alternator generates ac, while the dynamo generates dc
The alternator uses the motor effect, not induction

questions.explanation: The generator effect is used in an alternator to generate ac and in a dynamo to generate dc.

questions.stem: How does a microphone make use of the generator effect?

options.text: Variations in current are converted into pressure variations in the air
Sound shakes the magnet to and fro inside a coil that stays fixed
Sound waves are absorbed by a magnet, which then makes a current
Pressure variations in a sound wave are converted into variations in current

questions.explanation: Microphones use the generator effect to convert the pressure variations in sound waves into variations in current in electrical circuits.

questions.stem: What does a basic transformer consist of?

options.text: A primary coil and a secondary coil joined by a copper wire
Two coils wound on a solid copper core so charge passes easily across
A primary coil and a secondary coil wound on an iron core
A primary and secondary coil linked through the iron core carrying the current

questions.explanation: This is exactly the construction given in the specification.

questions.stem: A wire is moved through a magnetic field. The two ends of the wire are not connected to anything at all. What is induced in the wire?

options.text: Nothing at all, because the circuit around it is incomplete
A current, but no potential difference across the ends
A potential difference, but no current flows in the wire
Both a potential difference and a current in the wire

questions.explanation: A potential difference is induced across the ends of the conductor; a current is induced only if the conductor is part of a complete circuit.

questions.stem: A dynamo and an alternator have identical coils and magnets. Which part of the dynamo makes its output a direct current?

options.text: A split-ring commutator, which swaps the connections every half turn
A pair of slip rings, which keep the coil joined to the same contacts
A commutator that holds the output at one steady value
An iron core that stores the current between the half turns

questions.explanation: Swapping the connections each half turn keeps the output potential difference in one direction.
